top.title: Without manufacturing $1tr economy is an illusion
top.description: By Dele Sobowale Japan in fact offers a relevant historical example of what can happen to an economy which falls behind in the global manufacturing race. Even in Africa, the Giant of Africa is lagging behind at least three other economies in the scale and scope of manufacturing. Consequently, the politically-motivated promise to make Nigeria a one trillion dollar economy by 2030 is only one of the many illusions of the Tinubu administration. Desirable as it is, a $1 trillion economy is unachievable for reasons too numerous to discuss now, but, the cardinal reason is Nigeria’s weak manufacturing base – forcing us to import thousands of products which we can, with little effort, produce locally. I was a Senior Lecturer/Consultant working with the Nigerian Institute of Management, NIM, in 1992, when Morita wrote the article in which that statement was made. The NIM Library was my second home and office. When not busy teaching courses in Sales, Marketing and General Management, I was in the Library reading and gathering materials for my lectures, as well as my book of quotations, VBQ – which was published in 2007. Japan was the world’s second largest manufacturing economy as well as the second largest economy; and was threatening the American leadership in that regard. Several books were written on the Art of Japanese Management; leading American Business Schools included courses in Japanese business methods in their curricula as compulsory subjects. The Japanese economy was growing at 7 to 10 per cent annually; and projections were made regarding when it would overtake the US as the largest economy globally. China and India were nowhere in sight. Then, something happened. Science and technology brought new products which called for new and modern factories. Western investors, scared by Japan’s growing economic prowess, diverted investments to other Asian economies – South Korea, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and China. Gradually, several South East Asian nations started challenging Japan in sectors such as electronics and ship building. Unnoticeable at first, but the steady erosion of Japanese share of global manufacturing eventually took its toll. Today, the second and third leading manufacturers are China and India. China is now the largest manufacturer; hotly pursued by China. Japan has dropped to the fifth position in global ranking measured in terms of Gross Domestic Productivity, GDP. China, not Japan, is now threatening the US leadership. Manufacturing is the primary reason for that change in the fortunes of nations. top.description: The Nigerian naira opened Monday, November 16, 2026, under mild pressure across the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) while maintaining relative stability in the parallel market. top.description: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Steelers coach Mike McCarthy drops cryptic upate on DeShon Elliott injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers suffered a lopsided loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football , and head coach Mike McCarthy did not offer many answers on DeShon Elliott’s surprise absence afterward. Elliott was a late scratch for the 38-18 defeat in Cincinnati after injuring his knee during pregame warmups . When asked about the safety’s status after the game, McCarthy kept his update vague. “During his warm-up, he had something that showed up,” McCarthy said in a post-game press conference, via Chris Adamski of TribLive. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mike McCarthy on DeShon Elliott being a late scratch for what the team announced as a knee injury: “During his warmup he had something that showed up.” — Chris Adamski (@C_AdamskiTrib) November 16, 2026 It was a frustrating development for Elliott, who has been healthy for only two games this season and was expected to return to the lineup coming out of Pittsburgh’s bye week. Instead, he was ruled inactive shortly before kickoff. Pittsburgh was also without cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting, who was among the team’s inactives. The knee issue also brings back bad memories for the veteran defensive back. Last season, Elliott suffered a knee injury in a Sunday night loss to the Green Bay Packers that was expected to sideline him for the rest of the year, just months after he signed a two-year contract extension with the Steelers. Without Elliott, Pittsburgh’s secondary had no answers for Joe Burrow. The Bengals quarterback completed 35-of-44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns, two of which went to Chase Brown. Burrow threw three of those scores in the second quarter alone, sending Cincinnati into halftime with a 24-3 lead . The Bengals piled up 484 total yards and built a 31-3 lead before the Steelers found the end zone. Aaron Rodgers threw two late touchdown passes , one to DK Metcalf and the other to Pat Freiermuth, but the comeback attempt came far too late. Pittsburgh managed just 222 total yards. The loss snapped Pittsburgh’s four-game winning streak and dropped the Steelers to 6-3 on the season. McCarthy and the Steelers will now await more clarity on Elliott’s knee as they prepare to visit the Philadelphia Eagles next Sunday. top.title: 1,960 Flights Cancelled On Sunday Alone, As US Airport Disruption Enters Day Three
top.description: An additional 1,960 flights were cancelled on Sunday alone as the widespread disruption following an extraordinary no-takeoff order issued by US aviation authorities entered its third day on Monday. About 6,000 flights were cancelled at the weekend, leaving thousands of passengers stranded at airports. The ground stop issued Friday afternoon was only the second time such a directive had been issued nationwide in the busy US airspace since planes were grounded following the 9/11 attacks. It was blamed by the Trump administration on a faulty upgrade to communications equipment. As of Sunday evening, more than 55 US-related flights — those traveling within, into or out of the United States — scheduled for Monday were cancelled, according to industry tracker FlightAware. That marked a dramatic shift from the more than 1,960 flights cancelled on Sunday. Passengers wait for updates at a check-in area at Terminal 7 at Los Angeles International Airport, in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026. The Trump administration sought to reassure weary flyers as questions remained over how such chaos could unfold in the world’s largest economy, a country that prides itself on its technological prowess. Throughout the weekend, stranded passengers wandered through chaotic airports and sat on floors, waiting for updates or to be rebooked. Officials blamed Friday’s colossal snafu on faulty work to upgrade air traffic control communication cables. President Donald Trump on Sunday ended uncharacteristic days of silence on the ground stop, but only to blame his predecessor Joe Biden for the debacle. Planes sit idle at Los Angeles International Airport in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026. Trump insisted he inherited a mess from the Biden administration and said Congress, which his party has controlled for two years, must approve funds to upgrade America’s outdated air traffic control system. “The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster,” Trump said, referring to the Federal Aviation Administration. “Everything they touched turned bad. Big money spent unwisely, making an old and broken system worse than when they began,” Trump asserted. FAA chief Bryan Bedford had said Saturday that air travel for millions of Americans stranded at airports would return to normal by the close of business on Sunday. top.title: Evening at the improv? Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey make sure 49ers, fans enjoyed show
top.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey breaks away from the Dallas Cowboys defense for a 74-yard touchdown in the second quarter Sunday in Arlington, Texas. Tight end George Kittle (85) kept him clear of defenders. (Tom Fox/The Dallas Morning News) ARLINGTON, Texas - The offensive explosion began with improvisation. On Sunday, with the San Francisco 49ers trailing by six points and facing 3rd-and-8 at their 26-yard line, one play away from punting for the second time in their first four possessions, head coach Kyle Shanahan called a play in which wide receiver Keenan Allen was quarterback Brock Purdy 's first read. But Allen, running an in-breaking route nine yards downfield, was blanketed by cornerback Joey Porter. Purdy looked to his left to his second read, wideout Deebo Samuel . Nope. Covered. Meanwhile, Purdy's pocket was crumbling. Linebacker Shemar James blitzed. So did safety Caleb Downs. Purdy's internal clock went off. "I felt like I sort of had to get going," Purdy said. What happened next opened the floodgates in the 49ers' 46-40 win in which they gained 584 yards, the fifth-most in franchise history, and became the first team with three offensive touchdowns of 65-plus yards since 2000. As Purdy raced to his right, prepared to try to scramble for a first down, running back Christian McCaffrey made it a two-man improv act. McCaffrey's assignment on a play in which tight end George Kittle and wide receiver Jordan Watkins also ran routes didn't foreshadow glory. "He was in protection (blocking)," Shanahan said. Things changed. After McCaffrey leaned his right shoulder into defensive tackle Kenny Clark, he stopped for a split second, surrounded by three offensive linemen, before realizing Purdy was keeping the play alive. Scramble-drill mode. "It's just some backyard football," McCaffrey said. McCaffrey, in the middle of the field, near the line of scrimmage, initially broke to his right, into the flat, but he was running with James, who was chasing Purdy toward the sideline. McCaffrey instinctively cut upfield to daylight, splitting two defenders, just as Purdy had decided to try to run for the first down. "There's a point where it's like, ‘All right, I think I can try to use my legs now at this moment,'" Purdy said. "And I was going to do that." Things changed. At full speed, Purdy, seeing McCaffrey all alone around the 35-yard line, violently slammed on the brakes, just a yard away from crossing the line of scrimmage. "It's those little decisions that you make in games," McCaffrey said. "For Brock to not scramble - to not just surrender the play - but to keep it alive. That's a big deal." The Oklahoma City Thunder got back in the win column against the Sacramento Kings on Sunday, and rookie Aday Mara earned some high praise from head coach Mark Daigneault for his role in it. Mara posted a double-double with 16 points and 13 rebounds in 25 minutes off the bench as the Thunder cruised to a 125-103 win at Golden 1 Center. The 7-foot-3 big man shot an efficient 8-of-11 from the field and added three assists. After the game, Daigneault liked what he saw from the youngster , but he also made it clear that Mara cannot rest on one good night. top.title: Morgan Rogers starts as England beat the World Champions
top.description: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 15: Morgan Rogers of England competes for the ball with Marc Cucurella of Spain during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Spain and England at Wanda Metropolitano on November 15, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Manuel Queimadelos/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images) | Getty Images Morgan Rogers started while both sides fielded ex-Chelsea left backs in last night’s Nations League encounter at the Metropolitano in Madrid. Neither of those is likely to be the most memorable story from England’s impressive 3-2 win over the World Champions, but that’s what shook out from the Chelsea filter. It was in fact a direct matchup between Rogers and Marc Cucurella on England’s right, while on the left flank, former Academy standout Lewis Hall was having a good old time running forward with the ball. That was a bit of a theme for the Three Lions, having a good old time — at least until Elliot Anderson’s red card. Then it was shades of Mexico City, hanging on for the massive win. Thankfully, Jordan Henderson did not break his arm jumping over the advertising hoardings in celebration this time (probably because he wasn’t there). England, who came out with tremendous energy, built a scarcely believable three-nil lead at one point against the defending European and World Champions, with Harry Kane winning and scoring a penalty late in the first half, followed by a quickfire double from Ezri Konsa and Ben White as the game approached its hour mark. But then, Anderson made a very bad decision, giving away a penalty with a needless shirt-pull and getting sent off as well for not even attempting to play the ball, and from then on, it was hang-on time. Mikel Oyarzabal converted and Nico Williams scored just a few minutes after arriving on the scene to set up a grandstand finish. But we know how an inspired Tuchel team can rise to the occasion — even Rogers was defending! — and this was certainly a fine example of that. With the win, England are in the Nations League quarterfinals. Morgan Rogers played the full 90; he had no further comments about the Cole Palmer situation. Elsewhere, Roméo Lavia was back after sitting out Belgium’s last game due to suspension, and played 76 minutes in their 4-1 win over Marco Palestra’s Italy, 4-1. Mike Penders was an unused substitute as Belgium have now also qualified for the quarterfinals — finishing runners-up in their group to France, who beat Turkey, 2-1. Malo Gusto, after a performance that drew some rather terrible reviews last time out, was an unused substitute.

The veteran defensive tackle recorded 1.5 sacks that ended a lengthy drought and cleared out any doubts regarding his physical condition heading into the team’s bye week. Donald described his true emotions after the victory, particularly because the Rams’ defense spent relatively little time on the field. Donald finished Sunday’s game with an eight-game streak without one. He also moved past Justin Houston and Chandler Jones, who each finished their careers with 112 sacks, into 31st place on the NFL’s all-time list. The Rams’ defense delivered an impressive performance apart from just Donald’s individual numbers. Additionally, head coach Sean McVay praised Donald’s continued impact on the team. “I’m never surprised,” McVay said. “He never ceases to amaze me. I think the term ‘1 of 1’ is thrown around way too loosely this day and age, but it’s not with him. He’s 1 of 1.” The Rams have won four straight games after opening the season 2-4. top.description: Los Angeles Lakers v Phoenix Suns Getty Luka Doncic had 37 points through three quarters and figured his work was done for the afternoon. Instead, he had to check back in to help the Los Angeles Lakers finish off the Phoenix Suns. The Lakers won 131-123 on Sunday for their eighth straight victory, but Doncic used his postgame interview to tell his team what it needs to do better. “I wasn’t planning on playing in the fourth quarter; we need to get better at that. It was blamed by the Trump administration on a faulty upgrade to communications equipment. As of Sunday evening, more than 55 US-related flights — those traveling within, into or out of the United States — scheduled for Monday were cancelled, according to industry tracker FlightAware. That marked a dramatic shift from the more than 1,960 flights cancelled on Sunday. Passengers wait for updates at a check-in area at Terminal 7 at Los Angeles International Airport, in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026. The Trump administration sought to reassure weary flyers as questions remained over how such chaos could unfold in the world’s largest economy, a country that prides itself on its technological prowess. Throughout the weekend, stranded passengers wandered through chaotic airports and sat on floors, waiting for updates or to be rebooked. Officials blamed Friday’s colossal snafu on faulty work to upgrade air traffic control communication cables. President Donald Trump on Sunday ended uncharacteristic days of silence on the ground stop, but only to blame his predecessor Joe Biden for the debacle. Planes sit idle at Los Angeles International Airport in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026. Trump insisted he inherited a mess from the Biden administration and said Congress, which his party has controlled for two years, must approve funds to upgrade America’s outdated air traffic control system. “The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster,” Trump said, referring to the Federal Aviation Administration. “Everything they touched turned bad. nigeria.description: By Peter Egwuatu The Nigerian stock market rebounded last week after weeks of sustained pressure from profit taking led to decline in stock value. Similarly, another major market performance indicator, NGX All Share Index, ASI, surged by 1.4 % to close at 252,269.16 points from 248,877.22 points the previous week, indicating renewed demand for selected heavyweight stocks, which dominated the market. Analysts noted that although buying interests remained evident in major banking and industrial stocks , the broader market reflected a mixed trading pattern, with investors maintaining selective positions amid intermittent profit-taking in several stocks The positive performance, according to analysts, highlights the continued resilience of the domestic stock market, which has maintained substantial gains since the beginning of the year. Reacting to market performance and outlook analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited, said : “ The immediate market outlook remains cautiously positive, supported by the strong year-to-date return and continued interest in selected large-cap stocks. Nevertheless, investors are likely to maintain a selective approach, considering corporate earnings, dividend expectations, valuation levels and prevailing macroeconomic conditions before increasing their exposure. The possibility of further profit-taking cannot be ruled out, particularly in stocks that have recorded significant gains in recent sessions. Overall, the market appears to be consolidating its recent advances while maintaining an underlying bullish bias. The ability of the index to break above the 255,000-point resistance level, alongside improved market participation, will be important in determining whether the current upward movement can extend into another phase of appreciation.” They further noted that the political outcome of the US midterm elections introduced additional uncertainty into the market adding that the developments have placed renewed attention on the possibility of diplomatic negotiations and their implications for global crude supply. “For Nigeria, the movement in international crude prices remains particularly important given the country’s dependence on oil exports for foreign exchange earnings and government revenue. For many market women who rely on interstate commercial buses and trucks to restock goods such as foodstuffs, textiles, and household provisions, waybill logistics are the lifeline of daily commerce. However, traders said the shrinking grace periods before daily demurrage charges kick in have turned routine restocking into a financial burden. Mrs. Grace Okafor, a wholesale dealer in dried seafood and condiments, recounted how a 24-hour delay caused by heavy rainfall cost her nearly half of her expected profit on a recent consignment. “My goods arrived at the park late in the evening when no one could go out. “By the time I got there the next afternoon with a tricycle to carry my sacks, the park officials insisted I had exceeded their grace period and demanded N6,000 for ‘store keep’. “We cannot increase our selling prices because customers are already struggling to buy. That money came straight out of my capital.” Other traders noted that the lack of standardized billing across motor parks leaves them vulnerable to exploitation, particularly when unforeseen emergencies delay pickup. Mrs. Comfort Momoh, who trades in fabrics and wrappers, stated that arbitrary fee hikes are discouraging traders from ordering goods in bulk. “There is no fixed rate or clear receipt for this store keep money; it depends on the mood of whoever is on duty at the park store,” she said. “Sometimes a driver does not call on time to inform you that the vehicle has arrived, yet the park starts counting storage days against you. By the time you clear your bale, the profit is already gone.” Similarly, Alhaja Rasheedat Suleiman, a palm oil and grain merchant, called on market associations and transport unions to intervene and establish fair, transparent guidelines. “We understand that parks have limited space, but giving traders at least 48 hours of grace after proper notification is only fair,” Alhaja Suleiman said. “Most of us are breadwinners supporting our families from these stalls. nigeria.title: We demand impeccable voter register
nigeria.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, must urgently clean up its battered image by producing an impeccable voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general elections. The discovery that its own officials allegedly compromised the database through fraudulent registrations is a monumental embarrassment. It reinforces existing suspicions about the commission’s impartiality and competence at a time Nigerians desperately need an electoral umpire they can trust. The scale of the problem is alarming. Of the more than 11 million people registered during the 2026 Continuous Voter Registration, CVR, exercise, INEC’s Automated Biometric Identification System, ABIS, flagged approximately 1.5 million entries as suspicious. The commission subsequently removed 1,277,252 invalid records, leaving about 268,000 requiring further verification. The preliminary national register contains over 103.4 million voters. More disturbing is the alleged complicity of registration officers who abused their official login credentials to introduce fictitious identities. They reportedly uploaded AI-generated photographs, reused identical images and exploited registration provisions for persons with disabilities, claiming fictitious applicants had no fingers and could therefore bypass normal fingerprint verification. ABIS detected suspicious facial and biometric inconsistencies during screening. Artificial intelligence has consequently introduced a dangerous dimension toa electoral fraud. Its capacity to generate convincing human faces makes fabricating identities easier and visual inspection less reliable. Although digitally enhanced photographs of genuine applicants are not necessarily fraudulent, fictitious identities must be identified and eliminated. INEC says it has withdrawn implicated officers’ access credentials, commenced investigations, subjected suspicious entries to human adjudication and referred evidence for possible disciplinary action and prosecution. It promises further verification before the final register is displayed on December 15, 2026. These assurances are insufficient without demonstrable accountability. Public confidence in INEC was already fragile before this scandal. Controversies surrounding previous elections, particularly the disputed 2023 presidential election and the failure of IReV to upload results as expected, have deepened distrust. A manipulated register could facilitate fictitious voting identities, impersonation, inflated constituency figures and deliberate disenfranchisement of legitimate voters. Biometric accreditation may prevent some abuses, but cannot excuse a defective database. Professor JoashAmupitan must therefore open the corrective process to independent scrutiny. INEC should partner with opposition parties, civil society organisations, professional technology experts, the media and credible international electoral partners in conducting an independent forensic audit. The commission should publish state-by-state findings

nigeria.title: Nigeria: One-party or one-man state? By Suleiman A. Suleiman
nigeria.description: Since at least late 2024, when President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had been in office for barely 18 months, politicians and other Nigerians have been saying that the country is drifting into a one-party state. These warnings have not only grown louder in recent months; they are justified. The All Progressives Congress (APC) now controls 31 out of 36 states, since at least the middle of this year, when the 2027 election campaigns entered top gear. At the end of the 2023 election cycle, the APC controlled 21 states, including the off-cycle election in Edo State in 2024. This means that, in the last year, 10 sitting governors have defected from their original parties to join Tinubu in the APC. The reverse traffic, meanwhile, is zero. This is unlike the 2015 election cycle, when leading politicians were defecting from the then ruling People’s Democratic Party (PDP) to the then main opposition APC. At the same time, the transformation of political organisation and opposition parties that we witnessed during 2013–2015 does not appear to be happening this time, as the leading opposition parties remain ridden by crippling crises that President Tinubu and the APC have been accused of instigating. First of all, the PDP is now a one-man show, and it is difficult to even know what the party stands for or who its leading members are, other than FCT Minister Nyesom Wike. More significantly, in 2023, the Labour Party (LP) and the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) won 63 seats between them—almost all of them for the first time in history—in the National Assembly elections, and a total of 12 states and the FCT in the presidential election by their candidates, Mr Peter Obi and Dr Rabiu Kwankwaso, combined. That was a formidable performance, particularly by Peter Obi, but both the LP and the NNPP are no longer serious contenders in this election, and the two men have since left to meet on the same presidential ticket in the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). Accusing fingers also point to Tinubu for making their own political parties unviable platforms for the two men. This leaves the African Democratic Congress (ADC), which faces the most crisis of all. For almost a year, the ADC, formed by a partial coalition of like-minded and opposition interests, has been held hostage by the antics of one man, enabled almost entirely by Nigerian courts. The status of ADC candidates, from the presidential to the state assembly elections, currently hangs in limbo because Nigerian courts in this era now think that the dubious concerns of one party member are more important than the will of all the voters in the hundreds of primary elections conducted by the APC in the past months. In short, Nigeria today looks like a one-party state, with the ruling APC as the last man standing. In my view, however, Nigeria is not sliding into a one-party state. It is already a one-man state. nigeria.title: Businessman, Egungbohun charges African enterprises to connect across boundaries
nigeria.description: Businessman and Chairman of IBD Group, Chief Ibrahim Dende Egungbohun, has urged African entrepreneurs to build businesses that transcend national boundaries, strengthen regional trade and unlock the continent’s vast economic opportunities. Egungbohun made the call following his recognition by BusinessDay Newspaper at its Nigeria Business Leadership Awards (NBLA) 2026, in acknowledgement of his entrepreneurial achievements and IBD Group’s contribution to enterprise development across interconnected economic sectors. The ceremony, held on Friday, November 13, at Victoria Island, Lagos, also marked the newspaper’s 25th anniversary, themed “25 Years of Shaping Impactful Decisions.” Chief Egungbohun was represented by his wife, Chief Mrs Omolara Judith Egungbohun, Chief Executive Officer of IBD Hotels International and other members of the Group’s delegation included staff of IBD Hotels and representatives of IBD Foundation. In his nomination letter, BusinessDay Publisher and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Frank Aigbogun, commended IBD Group’s evolution from agriculture into a diversified enterprise with interests in logistics, construction materials, hospitality and energy. He observed that enterprise development extends beyond establishing businesses to building operating capacity, developing markets, sustaining commercial activities and creating institutions capable of enduring beyond individual transactions. In his remarks, Chief Egungbohun emphasised that Africa’s economic prosperity depended on connecting markets, strengthening commercial relationships and developing businesses capable of operating across geographical boundaries. He said: “Africa cannot unlock its full economic potential through isolated national markets. We must build enterprises that connect production, distribution, investment and trade across geographical boundaries. “At IBD Group, we see agriculture, logistics, hospitality, construction materials and energy as interconnected parts of a wider economic ecosystem. Their integration creates value chains, facilitates trade, attracts investment and generates employment. “Our ambition is to build businesses that contribute not only to national development but also to a more integrated African economy where entrepreneurs can compete, collaborate and create lasting value.” He dedicated the recognition to the Group’s employees, management, partners and stakeholders, acknowledging their collective contributions to its growth. His message resonates with Africa’s regional integration ambitions under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which seeks to expand intra-African trade and create opportunities for businesses across the continent. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. entertainment.title: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar Makes History as First Female Vice-Chancellor of UNIJOS
entertainment.description: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar, appointed as the 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor and first female Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jos. The University of Jos (UNIJOS) has officially appointed Professor Patricia Mamko Lar as its 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position since the institution was established in 1971. Announced on Thursday, 12 November 2026 by the university’s Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council, Senator Grace Folashade Bent , during a special meeting of the 15th Governing Council, the historic appointment sees Professor Lar succeed Professor Tanko Ishaya as she takes the helm of the Plateau State institution. Born in Langtang, Plateau State, Professor Lar is a distinguished Professor of Medical Microbiology whose career has been deeply woven into the fabric of UNIJOS for nearly four decades. After earning her Bachelor of Science degree in Microbiology from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria in 1986, she joined the University of Jos in 1987 as a Graduate Assistant in the Department of Medical Microbiology. She later went on to earn her Master’s degree in Medical Microbiology in 1989 and her PhD in Medical Parasitology in 1998 from the University of Lagos, followed by postdoctoral training at the Institute of Human Virology, University of Maryland in the United States under the NIH-Fogarty Fellowship Programme. Rising steadily through the academic ranks, she became an Associate Professor in 2012 before attaining full professorship in October 2015. Over the years, she has built an impressive body of work with more than 40 scholarly publications focusing on infectious diseases, including HIV/AIDS, malaria, antimicrobial resistance, and phytomedicine. Beyond the lecture hall and laboratory, Professor Lar has also served in key administrative roles at UNIJOS—including Head of the Department of Microbiology and Director of Linkages and Collaborations—and previously served a six-month tenure as Acting Vice-Chancellor of Yakubu Gowon University (formerly the University of Abuja) following her appointment by President Bola Tinubu in February 2025. Alongside her academic and leadership credentials, Professor Lar is a recognised advocate for women’s empowerment, having received the He4She Certificate of Award for Women Empowerment Activism in 2019. As she begins her five-year single term as UNIJOS’s first female substantive Vice-Chancellor after 55 years, she brings nearly four decades of institutional experience to the university’s top seat. entertainment.title: Ramla Ali Wins IBF and WBO Titles to Become Somalia’s First Boxing World Champion
entertainment.description: Unified world champion Ramla Ali poses in the ring with her WBO and IBF super-bantamweight belts and her coaching team in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram British-Somali boxer and fashion model Ramla Ali is officially a unified world champion! On 8 November 2026 at the College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, the 37-year-old athlete captured the vacant IBF and WBO super-bantamweight world titles after securing a split-decision victory over American contender Mikiah Kreps . During the ten-round bout, Ali dropped Kreps with a sharp right hand in the third round—the sole knockdown of the night—before two judges scored the contest 97–92 and 96–93 in her favour, against one scorecard of 98–91 for Kreps. With this triumph, Ali became Somalia’s first-ever professional boxing world champion and a unified titleholder in one unforgettable night. Born in Mogadishu, Somalia, she fled the civil war as a child with her family and grew up in East London, initially taking up boxing in secret as a teenager before turning it into a life-changing calling. Ramla Ali makes her ring walk behind the Somali and British flags ahead of her super-bantamweight world title fight in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Her remarkable journey from refugee to Olympic athlete and champion is also the subject of the biographical feature film In the Shadows. Directed by Anthony Wonke , the film premiered at the 70th BFI London Film Festival on 9 October 2026 before opening in UK and Irish cinemas on 30 October—just over a week before she lifted her world title belts in Texas. BAFTA-winning Top Boy actress Jasmine Jobson stars as Ali alongside Peaky Blinders actor Finn Cole as her husband and former coach, Richard Moore , with both Ali and Moore serving as executive producers on the project. This championship milestone builds on a string of barrier-breaking firsts across sports, cinema, and fashion. Long before her title win in Arlington, Ali made history as the first Muslim woman to win an English amateur boxing title, the first boxer to win an international gold medal while representing Somalia, and the first boxer to represent Somalia on the Olympic stage when she competed in the women’s featherweight division at the Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. The Pittsburgh Steelers suffered a lopsided loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football , and head coach Mike McCarthy did not offer many answers on DeShon Elliott’s surprise absence afterward. Elliott was a late scratch for the 38-18 defeat in Cincinnati after injuring his knee during pregame warmups . When asked about the safety’s status after the game, McCarthy kept his update vague. “During his warm-up, he had something that showed up,” McCarthy said in a post-game press conference, via Chris Adamski of TribLive. Instead, he was ruled inactive shortly before kickoff. Pittsburgh was also without cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting, who was among the team’s inactives. The knee issue also brings back bad memories for the veteran defensive back. Last season, Elliott suffered a knee injury in a Sunday night loss to the Green Bay Packers that was expected to sideline him for the rest of the year, just months after he signed a two-year contract extension with the Steelers. Without Elliott, Pittsburgh’s secondary had no answers for Joe Burrow. The Bengals quarterback completed 35-of-44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns, two of which went to Chase Brown. But Allen, running an in-breaking route nine yards downfield, was blanketed by cornerback Joey Porter. Purdy looked to his left to his second read, wideout Deebo Samuel . Nope. Covered. Meanwhile, Purdy's pocket was crumbling. Linebacker Shemar James blitzed. So did safety Caleb Downs. Purdy's internal clock went off. "I felt like I sort of had to get going," Purdy said. What happened next opened the floodgates in the 49ers' 46-40 win in which they gained 584 yards, the fifth-most in franchise history, and became the first team with three offensive touchdowns of 65-plus yards since 2000. As Purdy raced to his right, prepared to try to scramble for a first down, running back Christian McCaffrey made it a two-man improv act. McCaffrey's assignment on a play in which tight end George Kittle and wide receiver Jordan Watkins also ran routes didn't foreshadow glory. "He was in protection (blocking)," Shanahan said. Things changed. After McCaffrey leaned his right shoulder into defensive tackle Kenny Clark, he stopped for a split second, surrounded by three offensive linemen, before realizing Purdy was keeping the play alive. McCaffrey, in the middle of the field, near the line of scrimmage, initially broke to his right, into the flat, but he was running with James, who was chasing Purdy toward the sideline. McCaffrey instinctively cut upfield to daylight, splitting two defenders, just as Purdy had decided to try to run for the first down. "There's a point where it's like, ‘All right, I think I can try to use my legs now at this moment,'" Purdy said. "And I was going to do that." Things changed. sports.title: Morgan Rogers starts as England beat the World Champions
sports.description: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 15: Morgan Rogers of England competes for the ball with Marc Cucurella of Spain during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Spain and England at Wanda Metropolitano on November 15, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Manuel Queimadelos/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images) | Getty Images Morgan Rogers started while both sides fielded ex-Chelsea left backs in last night’s Nations League encounter at the Metropolitano in Madrid. Neither of those is likely to be the most memorable story from England’s impressive 3-2 win over the World Champions, but that’s what shook out from the Chelsea filter. It was in fact a direct matchup between Rogers and Marc Cucurella on England’s right, while on the left flank, former Academy standout Lewis Hall was having a good old time running forward with the ball. That was a bit of a theme for the Three Lions, having a good old time — at least until Elliot Anderson’s red card. Then it was shades of Mexico City, hanging on for the massive win. Thankfully, Jordan Henderson did not break his arm jumping over the advertising hoardings in celebration this time (probably because he wasn’t there). England, who came out with tremendous energy, built a scarcely believable three-nil lead at one point against the defending European and World Champions, with Harry Kane winning and scoring a penalty late in the first half, followed by a quickfire double from Ezri Konsa and Ben White as the game approached its hour mark. But then, Anderson made a very bad decision, giving away a penalty with a needless shirt-pull and getting sent off as well for not even attempting to play the ball, and from then on, it was hang-on time. Mikel Oyarzabal converted and Nico Williams scored just a few minutes after arriving on the scene to set up a grandstand finish. But we know how an inspired Tuchel team can rise to the occasion — even Rogers was defending! — and this was certainly a fine example of that. With the win, England are in the Nations League quarterfinals. Morgan Rogers played the full 90; he had no further comments about the Cole Palmer situation. Elsewhere, Roméo Lavia was back after sitting out Belgium’s last game due to suspension, and played 76 minutes in their 4-1 win over Marco Palestra’s Italy, 4-1. Mike Penders was an unused substitute as Belgium have now also qualified for the quarterfinals — finishing runners-up in their group to France, who beat Turkey, 2-1. Malo Gusto, after a performance that drew some rather terrible reviews last time out, was an unused substitute.

sports.title: Luka Doncic Sends A Message To Lakers After Suns’ Fourth-Quarter Rally
sports.description: Los Angeles Lakers v Phoenix Suns Getty Luka Doncic had 37 points through three quarters and figured his work was done for the afternoon. Instead, he had to check back in to help the Los Angeles Lakers finish off the Phoenix Suns. The Lakers won 131-123 on Sunday for their eighth straight victory, but Doncic used his postgame interview to tell his team what it needs to do better. “I wasn’t planning on playing in the fourth quarter; we need to get better at that. I know we played badly, we finished badly, but we need to improve in that area. When we manage to get ahead, we have to hold on to the lead, and we have to work on that.” Phoenix scored 43 points in the fourth quarter, matching Doncic’s total for the entire game. A lead that reached 31 in the third was down to five with just over a minute to play. By then, Doncic was back on the floor, and the Lakers still needed one more big shot. View this post on Instagram Luka Doncic returns as the Lakers’ lead shrinks The Lakers were up 101-70 with 1:47 to go in the third. They still had a 24-point cushion when the fourth began. Phoenix kept chipping away, and Lakers coach JJ Redick took a timeout with roughly five minutes left and the margin down to single digits. The Suns won the quarter 43-27. Doncic pointed to Phoenix’s increased aggression and said the Lakers got sloppy coming out for the fourth. He also took hold of the coaching whiteboard to address teammates during the game, according to Bleacher Report. Quentin Grimes gave Los Angeles breathing room in the final minute. With the Lakers ahead 126-121, he banked in a three to push the margin back to eight. Doncic added two free throws to close out the win. Grimes finished with 22 points, and Doncic paired his 43 with nine assists, per the box score. Lakers lean on Doncic with Austin Reaves out The Lakers played without Austin Reaves , who bruised his left heel in Milwaukee last week. Reaves entered Sunday averaging 24.7 points and 4.7 assists, leaving Los Angeles without one of its primary scorers and playmakers. Doncic put up 20 points in the first quarter alone. He made three shots from beyond the arc and went 7-for-8 from the line in those opening 12 minutes. Late in the third, he drew MVP chants in Phoenix after converting a three-point play. Phoenix was the last stop on a trip that took the Lakers through Detroit, Atlanta, and Milwaukee. Los Angeles had three days off after the Milwaukee game and finished the trip with a 12-2 record. Redick had credited the team’s offensive organization and disruptive defense during the winning streak while pointing to ball security and defensive rotations as areas that still needed work , as reported by the Los Angeles Times. He also said Reaves was improving and that his availability would come down to how much pain he could tolerate. Los Angeles returns home Tuesday to face the Charlotte Hornets at Crypto.com Arena. sports.description: 1 penalty saved, 3 stops, 100% run-outs: Man United keeper Senne Lammens regains form on international stage Manchester United had two players in international action on Sunday evening in a busy night of Nations League action. Senne Lammens The Belgian Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens has not had the best of seasons for Manchester United this year. Nonetheless, he has had a consistent run in the national team owing to Thibaut Courtois taking a break from international football after the World Cup. Lammens has been quite impressive in the group as his side finished second, one point behind France. According to SofaScore, he made three saves in their impressive 4-1 win over Italy, including a penalty stop in additional time at the end of the match. It’s been a canny week away from it all, in all honesty. Usually, I dread the international break, but for some reason I haven’t this time. Maybe it’s the relief of finally winning a game, coupled with the fact we’d played nine matches inside a month. It’s been a grueller, and we’ve been tremendously busy because of the sheer frequency of the fixtures. Whatever the reason, I think I’ve needed to switch off from it all (wey, to some extent). Quite a few people noted that I wasn’t my usual hyper self after we beat Chelsea. Thankfully we didn’t, and this conversation is completely different as a result, but a clean sheet and victory against one of the best teams in the league is a great start to what could be a much-needed resurgence. sports.title: LeBron James says he’s just done something he never thought he would do in his career
sports.description: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images LeBron James continues to make history in his 24th season in the NBA. The 41-year-old started for the Philadelphia 76ers in their 131-124 win against the Indiana Pacers on Sunday, and The King was in great form. James recorded 11 assists against the Pacers, and that took him past an iconic name in the all-time NBA assists charts. He says he never saw that coming. LeBron James says he didn’t foresee ranking third on the NBA career assists list James is one of the most complete players the NBA has ever seen. Over the course of his 24-year-long career, the four-time champion has played in all five positions on the court, and he has amassed incredible numbers under every metric. On Sunday, James took his career assists tally to 12,092, surpassing Hall of Fame point guard Jason Kidd to rank third on the list. That is an incredible achievement, one James says he is humbled by, but he has revealed that he never foresaw achieving this in his career. He said: “It’s super humbling. It’s something that I didn’t obviously foresee in my career. But I knew assists meant a lot to me. Just the movement of the ball, being able to find my teammates and put the ball on time and on target. “And also just being linked with some of the greats to have ever played this game, and also a dear friend of mine, J Kidd, is really special.” James now ranks third on the all-time assists list, below leader John Stockton, who recorded 15,806 career assists, and Chris Paul, who assisted 12,552 times. Ironically, James was on the Redeem Team of 2008 along with Kidd and Paul. He has overtaken one, and it now remains to be seen if he can do the same to the other before the end of this season. sports.description: Buffalo Bills edge rusher Leonard Floyd. Getty The Detroit Lions have a gigantic void to fill on defense after edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a season-ending injury, but could add a former Super Bowl champion as a bargain replacement. Hutchinson was hurt early in Sunday’s win over the New England Patriots, falling to the turf after leaping in the air while celebrating a sack of quarterback Drake Maye. Hutchinson was ruled out and is feared to have suffered a torn ACL, which would put him out for the season. Lions Could Grab Former Super Bowl Champion to Fill Defensive Void The Lions had already suffered another blow when linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a serious injury, and now may need to hit free agency to account for Hutchinson’s loss. While the Lions have yet to make an official statement on Hutchinson’s future, the injury is feared to keep him out for the remainder of the season. technology.title: Amazon loses first batch of broadband satellites launched on custom rocket
technology.description: Amazon’s ambition to operate a constellation of broadband satellites took a hit on Sunday, when 40 of its craft failed to make it into orbit. The failure is significant because it was the first Amazon launch to use a rocket designed especially for the job of carrying its broadband birds to low Earth orbit. The Lockheed/Boeing joint venture United Launch Alliance (ULA) created that rocket, a version of its Vulcan heavy lifter using a six-booster configuration and a Centaur V upper stage optimized to carry payloads into low Earth orbit. Last week, Amazon previewed the launch with a post that noted this mission, code-named LV-01, is the first of 38 planned missions with ULA, and that LV-02 would likely follow within weeks. The two companies planned to test new hardware on the first “several” flights using the custom rocket. Amazon put 40 satellites aboard the Sunday mission and said it is “already planning larger configurations for subsequent missions.” Those plans, and the LV-02 launch, are probably on hold after the rocket suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight. The flight began well, with the Vulcan reaching an altitude of 95 miles (150 km) and completing the first phase of its flight. Six minutes into the mission, the main booster and payload fairing both separated as planned, and ULA lit up the Centaur V’s engines for the first planned firings needed to reach low Earth orbit. Then came the anomaly, which UAL’s live update stream states meant the mission “failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit.” “Every flight generates data, and every flight teaches us something,” UAL wrote. “Since the anomaly just occurred, we don’t have any specific data yet to understand what occurred today.” Amazon already has over 200 satellites in orbit, had hoped to launch its satellite broadband service this year, and plans 20 or more launches in 2027. It is unclear if this mission failure will change those ambitions. ®

science.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 16 – NGC… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. NGC 7129: Star Formation with Jets from Webb Explanation: How do stars form? To help answer this question, NASA used the James Webb Space Telescope to take the featured detailed image of the star-forming region NGC 7129 in infrared light . Star formation progresses when gravity pulls together massive amounts of gas, but soon things can get complicated when previously formed stars emit powerful jets and winds — and some then explode . Opaque dust can form in the cool atmospheres of stars and, when dispersed, can obstruct visible-light images. Many stars can be seen to be forming in the featured image , with the young stars on the left, in the gold-colored gas, typically being more mature than the young stars on the right — in the red region. Jets and wind s likely cause the filamentary nature of the red-colored gas. Studying stars at different stages of development bolsters understanding about what physical processes are most important and when. It's a perfect evening… in 1996 or 2026. The entire concept of "Space Jam" is so '90s that you swear you can hear Los Del Rio in the background mouthing, "Dale a tu cuerpo alegría, Macarena." As ridiculous as an intergalactic basketball match may sound, it's a perfect example of how even the strangest idea can work if you commit to it fully. In case you thought you hallucinated the whole thing, no, you didn't, as the Looney Tunes find themselves in quite the predicament in this live-action-animation hybrid. A bunch of aliens known as the Nerdlucks arrive on Earth to abduct the Tunes and take them back as attractions to the outer-space amusement park known as Moron Mountain (shockingly nobody has claimed that subreddit, so do your thing, Internet!). Being a wheeling-and-dealing wabbit, though, Bugs Bunny proposes a winner-takes-all basketball game between the Tunes and the tiny Nerdlucks. Unfortunately, the crafty aliens use their tech to steal the talent from ballers like Charles Barkley and Muggsy Bogues and turn themselves into the scary and skilled Monstars. So, Bugs and friends reach out to Michael Jordan, who recently switched from basketball to baseball, to help the Tune Squad win this intergalactic b-ball matchup and their freedom, because if anybody can do it, Air Jordan (Hare Jordan?) can. Oh, Bill Murray also shows up here a few times. Why? Because he can! (Image credit: Warner Bros. Pictures) "Space Jam" is a spin on the classic sci-fi trope of resolving high-stakes conflicts through sports. In 1975, "Death Race 2000" introduced a world where people drive like hooligans and bash into each other to get ahead and win races (ironically, this is the regular experience on any public road now). Meanwhile, in the same year, "Rollerball" demonstrated how to use extreme sports as a plot device whereby brutality trumped any kind of skill in the arena. Yet "Space Jam" took this concept, cartoonified it for a family-friendly audience, and challenged the conflict resolution approaches of other alien invasion movies from 1996. While " Independence Day " saw the heroes trying to destroy the mothership and "Mars Attacks" featured humans running away from "Ack! Ack"-ing extraterrestrials with ray guns, this film used the court to settle the score. It's an innovative way to deal with interplanetary matters, that's for sure. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia
science.description: null On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds. When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use. Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) Why it mattered When the 300-foot telescope first debuted, it was not just the United States' largest radio observatory, but the largest such facility in the world. But its quick construction — just two years — led to it having to be significantly upgraded later. "In 1970, the 300-foot’s surface had become so warped from maintenance crews, snow, and its own weight that a new finer-meshed aluminum surface was installed," the website for the National Radio Astronomy Observatory reads. "A larger traveling feed was also installed at the prime focus." The collapse, however, was no one's fault. "Unforeseeable stress factors cracked a steel connector plate," wrote the NRAO. The Green Bank Telescope collapse left a mass of twisted debris behind. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) During its years of observations, the 300-foot telescope contirbuted to the discovery of dark matter and the realization that pulsars come from supernova explosions. "One of the most important products to come out of the 300-foot telescope was an all-sky survey of radio objects called the Green Bank 6cm Survey. Nearly every northern hemisphere radio object studied by any other telescope is from a catalog compiled using this telescope," reads the NRAO website. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: Why hasn't the 'Blaze Star' exploded yet? Astronomers weigh in on what to expect
science.description: null For the past two years, stargazers have waited with bated breath for a "new" light to appear in the night sky, born of one of the most cataclysmic events known to occur in the cosmos — a nova explosion. But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out. What is T. Coronae Borealis? T. Coronae Borealis — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold. Next comes a dramatic nova explosion that causes the star to flare to 1,000 times its usual brightness before gradually settling down and repeating the cycle. Why is it so challenging to predict T. CrB's nova flare? "T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon," Bradley Schaefer of the Louisiana State University Department of Physics and Astronomy told Space.com in an email. "Everyone is very confident on this. But we cannot make high-accuracy measures of the rate of gas falling onto the surface of the white dwarf, and we do not have a high accuracy measure of the trigger mass for the big hydrogen bomb." Schaefer continued. Historical observations reveal that the last nova eruption reached Earth in 1946, which places us well inside the window for another dramatic brightening of T. CrBb. However, the unpredictability of the white dwarf's feeding makes it difficult to pin down exactly when the explosion will become visible from Earth. An animation of T. CrB brightening. (Image credit: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center Conceptual Image Lab) "The exact date of the upcoming T CrB eruption depends primarily on how fast the gas coming from its companion star is accumulating on the surface of the white dwarf," explained Schaefer. "When some specific trigger mass has accumulated, then T CrB will erupt. For the last 80 years, we have been watching the gas pile up on the white dwarf surface, and we know that it must be near the trigger threshold." Astronomers have tried to predict T CrB's brightening by comparing a recent fluctuation in the light of the distant star system to a similar event that occurred in the runup to the 1946 event. "There have already been some dimming and brightening episodes that caused excitement but did not yet turn into the main event," Elizabeth Hays, lab chief at NASA's Astroparticle Physics Laboratory at the Goddard Spaceflight Center , told Space.com in an email. "It is likely that the nova will happen in the next few years but we still don't know exactly when. I can't give you a guaranteed prediction, but I will be a little surprised if it gets to 2030, or 84 years past the last eruption." science.title: How escaping gases ripped apart a comet and caused it to become thousands of times brighter
science.description: A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times. Comet 220P/McNaught was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the sun as Mars . Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year. On June 14, as it headed towards perihelion – the closest point in its orbit to the sun, at a distance from our star of 1.5 times the distance between the Earth and the sun (known as an astronomical unit) , 220P suddenly and without warning burst into life. On 31 May, the comet was languishing at magnitude +17.39 (the higher the magnitude, the fainter an object is), but within less than 14 hours it had dramatically brightened to magnitude +11.05, bringing it into range for observation with small amateur telescopes. By June 2, 220P was up to magnitude +8.23 and was technically visible for a short while in 10x50 binoculars from a dark site, prompting amateur astronomers and astrophotographers to chase down this rare event. By perihelion, the comet had faded back to magnitude +12, but more was to come. A second outburst began at the end of July, brightening from magnitude +14 on 28 July to magnitude 6.1 by 6 August. Telling the tale of a dirty snowball Comets are often referred to as dirty snowballs, and beneath their dusty crust are ices made from various volatiles, including water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen. Solar heating, even at the distance of Mars, can cause these ices to rapidly sublimate into gases, and the pressure of the escaping gas rips the surface apart, spewing huge amounts of dust in to space. Models based on observations of 220P’s outburst indicate that it spewed out between tens of billions and hundreds of billions of pounds’ worth of cometary dust that filled the comet’s coma, the diffuse 'atmosphere' that clings to the comet’s solid nucleus. The dust particles, which are just millionths of a meter across, expanded outwards from the comet at about 1,280 feet (390 meters) per second, scattering sunlight and causing the coma to substantially brighten. "We have concluded that the comet detached localized parts of its crust, creating a dust-rich envelope that increased [the comet’s brightness by] 250 times in half a day," Josep M. Trigo-Rodríguez, of the Institut de Ciències de l’Espai and the Institute of Space Studies of Catalonia in Spain, said in a statement . science.title: What's next for SpaceX's Starship after epic Flight 15 chopsticks catch?
science.description: null Starship may have just made history, but it still has some work to do to get fully up and running. The megarocket launched on its 15th test flight on Friday (Nov. 13), aiming to pull off a dramatic and unprecedented twofer. SpaceX wanted to bring both Starship elements — its Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — back to the launch pad at its Starbase site in Texas to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. It didn't happen with Super Heavy; the booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday evening after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship came home successfully , nestling into the tower's arms in a soft and unprecedented embrace on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after lifting off. Long-distance view of Ship's historic landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on three test flights to date. But it had never caught a Ship before; indeed, it had never even tried before Saturday. It's tougher and riskier to catch Ship; the upper stage flies much higher and faster than Super Heavy, so its return trip is much more more involved. Saturday was therefore a very big day for the company. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel," SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." The F light 15 mission plan gave us a sneak peek at the future: The double catch will be standard on operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will enable rapid inspection, refurbishment and reflight of the megarocket, according to SpaceX. And the company is indeed planning on rapid reflight. Elon Musk has said that SpaceX is targeting 10,000 Starship launches per year by 2030, which works out to more than one liftoff every hour on average. Why such a mind-boggling cadence? Because SpaceX plans to build megaconstellations far larger than anything circling Earth today. For example, it wants its next-gen Starlink V3 broadband network to consist of 100,000 satellites . And its planned Starmind AI data-center constellation will be 10 times bigger than that, featuring one million spacecraft , if all goes to plan. For perspective: SpaceX's current-gen Starlink network in low Earth orbit (LEO), by far the largest constellation ever assembled, is about 11,000 strong at the moment. A look at the 33 Raptor engines of Starship's Super Heavy booster during the vehicle's Flight 15 test launch on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Josh Dinner, Space.com/Future) Rocket recovery is only part of the reuse equation, of course; there's also refurbishment and reflight. And that gets us back to the "work left to do" discussion, for SpaceX has yet to demonstrate rapid reflight with either Super Heavy or Ship. science.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever (video)
science.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? SpaceX had already caught Super Heavy — on three previous Starship test flights, in fact. But it had never tried before with Ship. The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. Ship 42 comes in for its landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) While the double-catch attempt, and the chopsticks success with Ship, were Flight 15's main headlines, the mission had other objectives as well. One was getting Ship to orbit, which had happened on just one previous Starship launch — Flight 14 , which lifted off on Sept. 28. Ship deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) on Flight 14, and it did so again on Flight 15.
